html:
SMTO-RST-0016 — Two parts of SMTO tried to run the same task

GUID: 1480aebf-bbb3-497c-92d2-707a69169791
Slug: run-owner-active
Domain: RST · Subsystem: rst

What happened

  • While this task was running, a second part of SMTO tried to take it over, so the second one stopped. The task may still be running, or it may have stopped partway.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Refresh the page and open the conversation again to see the task's live progress. The task usually still has one part of SMTO working on it, and refreshing reconnects you to it.
  2. If the task is still working, wait for it to finish instead of sending the same request again. Losing the connection doesn't mean the work stopped, and sending it again could run it twice.
  3. If the task shows as stopped, read its last messages and check what it already changed before selecting Continue task. Some of its commands may already have run, and Continue task should only pick up what is left.

What success looks like

  • The task shows its live progress again, or it finishes and shows a result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start a second copy of the same task while the first one may still be running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run's saved control_error records an owner-active conflict (runtime.owner_active): another owner held the run when this attempt tried to drive it; current code only reads this to repair proven historical partial runs.

What this means

  • The retained owner-active diagnostic denotes a competing run owner; current code recognizes it specifically when repairing proven historical arbitration failures. State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.

Why this can happen

  • The retained owner-active diagnostic denotes a competing run owner; current code recognizes it specifically when repairing proven historical arbitration failures.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current ownership rather than assuming an old persisted owner-active message proves a worker is still alive.

How to fix it

  • Reconnect to the run's existing progress stream if an owner is live. For a historical partial run whose control_error contains runtime.owner_active, lifecycle_projection.repair_legacy reopens it to waiting_job only when required background jobs are known and no stop, pause, continuation or unknown operation exists; otherwise inspect the run's jobs and effects before using Continue task.
  • Reconnect to the current owner when present; use supported recovery for a proven historical ownership conflict.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The current owner is observed or supported recovery resolves the historical conflict without duplicate execution.

What not to do

  • Do not treat a lost connection as proof that earlier remote work did not run.

Technical notes

  • State diagnostics preserve authoritative journal, ownership and effect evidence. They do not delete records, loosen ownership fences, issue SQL or restart/replay work; missing persistence confirmation is separate from in-memory acceptance.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
